Definition: of uncertain affinity; sweet (i.e. not bitter nor salt):--sweet, fresh.
BiblicalUsage: glykýs is the word for sweet, fresh. In James 3:11, the text says "Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet [water] and bitter?" In James 3:12, the text says "figs? so [can] no fountain both yield salt water and fresh."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: glykýs tells me that creation is God's handiwork, and it still speaks of Him to anyone willing to look. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
